clue.text: Unorthodoxy about deception by fellow involved in terrible crime, not the first

indicators.note: the group of short pieces is described as caught up inside the crime word, so they are placed within it
the crime word is to lose its opening letter before anything goes into it

parts.note: an enormity is a monstrous or terrible crime
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject
a con is a trick or deception
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: Someone's heresy concerns a fraud by a fellow mixed up in a dreadful crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' trims ENORMITY to NORMITY; 'involved in' then puts ON, CON and F after its first letter: N + ONCONF + ORMITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Failure to follow accepted beliefs or practices is unorthodox behaviour, i.e. refusal to conform.

clue.text: Prominent programme on location with variety of virtues

parts.note: an OB, outside broadcast, is a programme made on location rather than in the studio

indicators.note: a variety of the word virtues means its letters in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A notable broadcast from somewhere out of the studio covers many different virtues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges VIRTUES into TRUSIVE, placed after OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obtrusive sticks out noticeably, as anything prominent does.

clue.text: Fellow catches echo, low

indicators.note: the fellow word is said to catch the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
Echo is the radio alphabet code word for E

explanation.surface: A man hears his voice bounce back, faint and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like describing the echo's volume, but it is the definition: low as in cheap and nasty, or low in price.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap can mean contemptible or vulgar, a sense shared with low, as in a cheap or low trick.

clue.text: Catch including lakelet's last good carp

indicators.note: the catch word includes, i.e. holds within it, the following pieces

parts.note: to nick someone is to catch or arrest them

indicators.note: only the final letter of lakelet is taken

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is the usual crossword abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A fisherman lands a decent carp at the far end of a little lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' is the fish in the surface, but here it is the verb: to find fault pettily.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain about trivial details, which is what a fussy fault-finder does.

clue.text: Back of head, caught on film that's turned up, getting covered by old hat

indicators.note: the inner pieces are covered by the old-hat word, i.e. sit inside it

parts.note: something old hat is out, out of fashion
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the film word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pic is a picture, a film

explanation.surface: Someone shot on camera from behind, wearing an old-fashioned hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses PIC to CIP; C + CIP then goes inside OUT: O + CCIP + UT.
explanation.definitionFit: The occiput is the anatomical name for the rear part of the skull.

clue.text: Rule badly muddled initially, good in revised version

indicators.note: only the opening letter of muddled is used
the letter for good goes in the middle of the rearranged word
a revised version is a rearranged one, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A chaotic first draft becomes a good one once it is rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' turns VERSION into ISOVERN; 'in' puts G inside it (ISGOVERN), after M from 'muddled initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: To misgovern is to govern a country poorly, ruling it badly.

clue.text: Walk from vehicle quietly

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone gets off a tram and quietly walks away.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk a long way with heavy steps, a trudging walk.

clue.text: Part of building containing diamonds one can look through?

definitions.text: Part of building containing diamonds one can look through?

parts.words: Part of building containing diamonds one can look through?
parts.note: suggests a jeweller's display, but the diamonds are diamond-shaped panes set in a criss-cross frame of glazing

explanation.surface: A jeweller's shop window displaying gems to passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a casement has small diamond-shaped panes held in a crossed framework of lead strips.

clue.text: Yield ringing praise on conclusion of variations penned by hard-working composer

indicators.note: the yield word rings, i.e. encircles, the praise word

parts.note: to cede is to yield or give up
to laud is to praise

indicators.note: the closing letter is penned, enclosed, by the hard-working word

parts.note: busy means occupied and hard-working

indicators.note: only the final letter of variations is used

explanation.surface: A diligent composer writes variations ending in a submissive, adulatory flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' puts LAUD inside CEDE (CLAUDEDE); 'penned by' puts S inside BUSY (BUSSY); 'on' simply places one part after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Debussy was the French composer of La Mer and Clair de lune, a leading Impressionist.

clue.text: Article carried by BBC mostly about being reliable

indicators.note: the article is carried within the shortened nickname, so it goes inside
most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: Auntie is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC
the is the definite article
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A news item broadcast on the BBC, mostly concerning trustworthiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts AUNTIE to AUNTI; 'carried by' puts THE in it after AU: AU + THE + NTI, then C.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authentic is genuine and can be trusted, as anything dependable can.

clue.text: Delay taking seat in church

definitions.meaning: to put off or play for time
an enclosed seat in a church choir or chancel

explanation.definitionFit: Play for time, a verb, and a choir seat in a cathedral chancel, a noun, share one spelling.

clue.text: Time to carry box

parts.note: to hump is to carry something heavy with effort

explanation.surface: It's time to lug a crate somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like the crate being carried, but it is the verb: box as in punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To box someone's ears is to hit them, and a hard blow with the fist is a heavy punch.

clue.text: Unrehearsed part in concert beginning to unravel after one minute

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

indicators.note: only the opening letter of unravel is taken

explanation.surface: An improvised section of a concert starts to fall apart a minute in.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in answer order: 'after one minute' puts I and M first, then PROM, PT and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done on the spur of the moment, without preparation or practice.

clue.text: Member of tribe with energy leading retreat

indicators.note: the energy word leads, coming before the retreat word

parts.note: chi (or qi) is the vital energy of Chinese philosophy
a nook is a secluded corner, a retreat

explanation.surface: A tribesman has the energy to lead a withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinook are a Native American people of the Pacific Northwest, so one of them belongs to that tribe.

clue.text: Banner, formal, I'm getting organised to go over middle of red…

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are reorganised into a new order
only the central letter of red is taken

explanation.surface: A formal flag, which I am arranging to cover the red middle part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting organised' rearranges FORMAL and IM into ORIFLAMM; 'go over' puts E, the middle of 'red', inside: ORIFLAMME. The ellipsis joins the clue to 17 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the red-gold battle standard of early French kings, hence any rallying flag.

clue.text: See Lear etc wrongly portrayed as a result of refining work?

indicators.note: the letters are portrayed in a wrong order, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch King Lear and so on badly acted, as if after polishing work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear etc' suggests Shakespeare; the question mark flags the definition: refining sugar leaves a dark syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark syrup is a by-product of the sugar refinery, drained from sugar during processing.

clue.text: … carpet, one you'll see actors on before entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue the actors word sits on top of the word for one
the word for entrance comes after the others

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Continuing 15: the red carpet, which you'll see stars walk on before going in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is the red carpet of the surface, but is the verb here: to reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to call them in and rebuke them severely, a stern telling-off.

clue.text: Small waterbird, very lost, less strong

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: the very letter is lost, removed from the bird

parts.note: a diver is a diving water bird, a loon

explanation.surface: A little water bird, much lost, is feebler than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' drops V from DIVER to leave DIER, after WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Weedy means thin and feeble, so weedier is comparatively feeble.

clue.text: Nonsense connected with a trial endlessly goes around

parts.note: rot is nonsense

indicators.note: the trial word loses its final letter

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Rubbish linked with a test that never finishes keeps going round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rotates turns on an axis, spinning round.

clue.text: Skill and force with batting 5 shown by county, apart from tail

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
in cricket the side batting is in

indicators.note: the county is taken without its final letter

parts.note: Essex is an English county east of London

explanation.surface: Skill and power from the number five batter in the county side, except at the end of the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 in the clue gives no letters; 'apart from tail' cuts ESSEX, an English county, to ESSE, after F and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is refined delicacy and skill in handling something.

clue.text: Student less bound by rules about silence

indicators.note: the comparative word goes about, i.e. around, the silence word

parts.note: freer means less restricted
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A student, less tied down by regulations, is around the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresher is a first-year undergraduate at a British university.

clue.text: Story from a long time back containing verse with a lot of character

indicators.note: the reversed time word holds the verse letter inside it
the time word is read back, backwards

parts.note: an eon is an immeasurably long time

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a letter is a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An old tale in verse, full of colourful personalities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EON into NOE; 'containing' puts V inside (NOVE); 'a lot of' cuts LETTER to LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, a light romantic or sentimental story.

clue.text: Covers story up, against screening it

indicators.note: the word for against screens, enclosing, the reversed story

parts.note: vs, versus, means against

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the story word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib

explanation.surface: Lies are hidden away, with someone opposed to screening them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LIE into EIL; 'screening it' puts that inside VS.
explanation.definitionFit: Veils are coverings for the face, so as a verb they cover things over.

clue.text: Poem declared towering tour de force?

indicators.note: spoken out, so the words are said and heard as something else

parts.note: towering means high; a coup is a brilliant stroke, a tour de force

explanation.surface: A poem was proclaimed a lofty masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH plus COUP (said 'koo') sounds like the poem's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a Japanese form of verse of three lines and seventeen syllables.

clue.text: Agitated during dispute, hackles rising

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the answer lies during, within, the run of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone gets worked up during an argument, hackles going up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Agitated during' as the definition; 'during' is the signal for the concealed letters, so the definition is 'Agitated' alone. 'rising' reads PUTEH upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is informal British for anxious or excited, worked up.

clue.text: element getting rid of leader displaying hatred

indicators.note: the element's name loses its first letter

parts.note: sodium is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A substance discarding its chief shows loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is widespread hatred or disgust directed at someone.

clue.text: Volunteers with success blended in as island dwellers

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
a hit is a success

indicators.note: the letters are blended together into a new mix

explanation.surface: Volunteers are a hit, mixing in as residents of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blended' turns IN AS into IANS after TA and HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahitians are the people of Tahiti, an island of French Polynesia.

clue.text: Seller, making return, succeeding when companies stumble?

definitions.text: Seller, making return, succeeding when companies stumble?

parts.words: Seller, making return, succeeding when companies stumble?
parts.note: describes a financier who profits by buying ailing firms and selling off their holdings piecemeal

explanation.surface: A trader who profits when businesses get into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a raider buys a struggling company cheaply and sells its property and plant for gain.
